questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had spent 2 years being heavily theory-focused and wanted to go somewhere where I could take electives that were interdisciplinary and applicable and based on “real world” cases. The “Bristol Futures” courses fit that bill.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of very informative e-mails and a very accessible support office for study abroad students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I got an e-mail with a link to their registration website, where i filled out a form with the necessary documents attached. Very standard and not that demanding a process.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy through the university, but nerve-wracking. you can only get one offer so you kind of have to accept the one you get...  But I heard that private accommodation was an absolute nightmare and twice the price.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living near green spaces Is lovely. the city center can feel quite busy, so I would say that the extra transportation time is worth it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The catering at the catered accommodation is really bad. And if it's good, then you WILL get sick of eating  the same thing for 5 months. Go self-catered,

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got an e-mail with a link to their registration website, where i filled out a form with the necessary documents attached. Very standard and not that demanding a process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Support over e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I got all of my first choices

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don’t leave it to the last minute. Find all the necessary documents beforehand.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It felt like you very easily could get away with doing the bare minimum if you wanted too. And the engagement from the other students was also very low during class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures felt very impersonal, even if they were only 20 students in class. The teachers didn’t really engage with the students. A very “Podcast-style” of teaching. The seminars where very quiet -  nobody wanted to participate in the group work or if they did they. were scared to share their thought to the broader classroom.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Histories: Possible Pasts and Alternative Futures
Understanding Global Problems Using Data: inequality, Climate Change and the Economy
Sustainable Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked Global histories seminars and assignments – they were very fun and creative. I have been told that the Bristol Future courses have a reputation for being easier than other more demanding courses. It didn’t necessarily sound that way when comparing experiences with other exchange students, but that is the narrative around them.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Expensive accommodation and expensive transportation. Public transportation was quite expensive – about as expensive as in Denmark I would say.  The accommodation I ended up with was also way above my original budget.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Compared to DK the have cheap sweets, meats and drinks 

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: VERY! Bristol has a lot of societies – if you can imagine it, they have it. I was a member of the Cheese Society, which was interesting and delicious.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Study Abroad office did a lot of great events for exchange students. Trivia nights at pubs, bowling and various social mixers. A ton of other event planned by the various societies as well – masquerade balls, croquis, hiking trips etc etc etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Daytrips planned the Global Lounge to various cultural sites or cities were very nice, since they sometimes can be quite a journey to get to otherwise. Plus you get to spend the day socialising with people also on exchange and make new friends or bond with your current ones  Also just keep an eye on the Student Union website, where all the societies post about their upcoming event – ticket for non-members are usually 3 gbp

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Stonehenge and Windsor Castle are a must, I think. The Lake district is absolutely beautiful as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Generally there isn’t a significant difference in culture, except maybe for talking to strangers.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join student societies. Just show up and you’ll be grand

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Pubs :) pints, fish and chips and good times. 
The street art in Bristol is also quite unique.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1)	Just show up. Show up tired, alone, wired or whatever. Both regarding the social and academic engagements. 
2)	Don’t worry too much about what everybody else’s exchange stay looks like online. It can be easy to feel boring or like you’re wasting your stay by not travelling a bunch, but I liked immersion myself locally, rather than always being off to the next place the first chance I got. 
3)	If possible, try to leave room in your budget for the unexpected fun stuff. Its not fun to always think about money first when you get invited to out with new friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the Global Lounge! It’s an amazing opportunity to have a “third space”.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I made a friend whom i really like   In the end i found that exchange was more about the people and connections you make during your stay, more so than the culture or academics. Its worth investing properly in those relationships during your stay.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Groupwork and budgeting – i didnt do much of either succesfully.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
